- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 5%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1-2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates late-period prices (last 7-10 days); apply downward adjustment of 0.5–1.5% per day for the final 7 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; apply a 2-day “sentiment catch-up” adjustment to forecast.
